corrected_draft.title: Federal Bureau of Prisons Issues First Step Act and Second Chance Act Directive
corrected_draft.description_short: In June 2025, the Bureau of Prisons issued a directive concerning implementation of the First Step Act and Second Chance Act.
corrected_draft.description_medium: In June 2025, the Federal Bureau of Prisons issued a directive concerning implementation of the First Step Act and Second Chance Act. The bureau described the directive as supporting implementation of both laws. This is inconsistent with the entry’s claim that all non-security rehabilitation programming had ended in March. The narrower directive is a documented event, but it does not establish the status of every program at every facility.
corrected_draft.description_long: In June 2025, the Federal Bureau of Prisons issued a directive addressing implementation of the First Step Act and the Second Chance Act. The bureau said the memorandum would treat First Step Act earned-time credits and Second Chance Act eligibility as cumulative and stackable for qualifying prisoners. It also said conditional placement dates should guide referrals, that stable housing and readiness for community reintegration should guide placement decisions, and that residential reentry center bed-space limits should not bar home confinement when a person is statutorily eligible. BOP described the change as intended to reduce unnecessary incarceration, ease strain on prison bedspace and staffing, and permit home confinement for qualified people with stable housing and community ties. Director William Marshall said the directive was intended to remove barriers to community placement. These are the bureau’s stated aims, not independently measured results. The announcement describes a June policy directive aimed at implementation of both statutes.
